thread:
maria: quick summary — after the kernel-selection tweak landed yesterday, I ran an nsys+perfetto capture on srv-12. Observed ~1.6x 95th latency regression for batch_size=4 on the 7B workload.

sam: ugh. any obvious hotspots?

maria: timeline shows an extra kernel launch per token and multiple short memcpy spikes between kernels. NVTX spans look like batcher -> kernel-selector -> launch -> wait -> kernel.

lee: can you drop the before/after timelines side-by-side? a flame or perfetto trace snippet helps.

maria: uploaded both traces to S3: s3://redwood-perf/traces/2034509876/after.nsight and s3://redwood-perf/traces/2034509000/before.nsight. perf-bot posted the short diff summary below.

perf-bot: nsys diff report: https://perf.redwood/reports/2034509876-diff (auto-generated). Key findings: +14% kernel-launchs, +30% memcpy stalls on H2D, increased host->device queue stalls.

sam: the kernel-selector change was supposed to favor smaller kernels for memory locality, right? maybe it's choosing a suboptimal kernel for this seq-len distribution. Maria, which commit touched selector heuristics?

maria: looks like commit 9b7c4f3 (runtime/selector: prefer tiled_256 for L>128) — that's the one. I ran a quick bisect locally: reverted that diff and the tail latency goes back to baseline.

lee: interesting. so behavior = more launches because tiled_256 has shorter per-kernel time but more kernels overall = extra host sync overhead?

maria: exactly. nvtx shows extra host->device synchronizations between tiled kernels. Batcher is splitting sequences differently after selector change, losing opportunity for continuous KV cache reuse.

sam: can you paste the minimal repro command you used so infra can reproduce?

maria: sure — command I used:
```
nsys profile --output after --sample=none --trace=nvtx,cuda python -m inference.bench \
  --model redwood-7b --batch-size 4 --seq-len 256 --warmup 20 --steps 200
```

lee: thanks. next steps: 1) perf-team to run the same with a micro workload (single-threaded) to confirm host queue stalls; 2) try forcing previous kernel policy to verify fixed; 3) open regression ticket with bisect evidence and traces.

sam: I'll create the ticket and assign to @maria. include the nsys diff link and both traces. Also ping infra to reserve srv-12 for a repro run. :+1:

maria: noted — I'll attach the bisect log and a short perf-note explaining KV-cache invalidation pattern we saw. Also trying a perfetto flame to highlight memcopy timing.

lee: one more thing — check batching heuristics too. if selector change altered observed sequence boundaries, batcher might be emitting smaller sub-batches. That plus tiled kernel fragmentation is a 2x effect.

maria: good call. I'll add a small script to log batcher split sizes during the run and attach.

sam: perfect. please post updates in this thread after ticket creation. :thinking_face:

maria: will do — creating ticket now and uploading artifacts.
